about: E1 (docs/plans/p2_final_plan.md, amendment 2; report only, no-ship): EmpMean (the organisers' empirical mean, baselines_p1 'empmean') and 1PL-ship (the plain 1PL at LEVEL, baselines_p1 'rasch') on P1a's READING, AUDIT, MIXTURE and FLAT runs (seed 11, runs 0-79, split scope 'pair'), paired with ship on P1a's stored rows; TUNED 0-79 re-scored as the control against baselines_p1. D is comparator minus ship (positive: hier-ship better); SEs run / cluster (parent, subject) / parent-stratified, level_calibration.Boot with 2,000 resamples, seed 0. Run history (disclosed): a dry run on 6 tasks, with an earlier scoring block, preceded the scored run, and its rows were discarded. The scored run (2026-10-06, rows written 18:55 to 18:59 UTC by script sha16 8a8535cf3391aa85, scoring block 8b9afc6e589cbad3...) kept its rows in a session scratch directory under /private/tmp, which the machine's restart cleared. On 2026-10-07 the 400 tasks were scored again into the default rows directory by the same scoring block (rows.regimes.*.script_sha16 names the script); every regime's scored_values_sha256 and every run's per_run_sha16 equal the first run's, so every statistic here is the first run's bit for bit. Only the timings (configs' mean_call_ms and max_call_s, rows.regimes.*.utc, task_s_*, max_rss_gb) are the second scoring's.
commands: python experiments/e1_baselines_rs.py score --shard k/3   (k = 0, 1, 2; repeat while it exits with 75)

plan.pythonhashseed: the two configs' rows do not depend on it: baselines_p1.Maker builds parents in sorted order and neither config keeps an EB trace

TUNED.source: E1 summary.regimes.TUNED.vs_ship.empmean (re-scored control, equal to baselines_p1's)
E1 summary.regimes.TUNED.vs_ship.rasch (re-scored control, equal to baselines_p1's)

rows.note: rows are row files as baselines_p1 writes them, one a task; a directory outside the repository is temporary. Re-scoring reproduces them bit for bit: each regime's scored_values_sha256 covers EXACT_FIELDS of both configs on every run, not the timings
